svg.title: Traversing a 4 by 4 column-major Fortran array with the first subscript innermost (consecutive memory) and with the second subscript innermost (jumps of four elements)
svg.text: Loop order against column-major storage: real a(4, 4)
the number in each cell is the step at which a loop nest visits it; the strip on the right is the array in memory
Column-wise: do j / do i, the first subscript innermost
consecutive steps touch neighbouring elements: stride 1, every byte of a cache line is used
memory, first element on the left; each bracket is one cache line (drawn with 4 elements, a real 64-byte line holds 8 doubles)
Row-wise: do i / do j, the second subscript innermost
consecutive steps are four elements apart (stride = the extent of the first dimension): one element per line is used
memory, first element on the left; each bracket is one cache line (drawn with 4 elements, a real 64-byte line holds 8 doubles)
With a 4096 by 4096 array of double precision values the stride is 32 KiB, so each step of the row-wise nest lands on a different cache line and page.
